fact_check_log.claim: Takeaway 2: when the celebrant is not a minister of religion, it is sufficient for each of you to say the s45(2) words, or words to that effect, in front of the celebrant and witnesses.
As at November 2026, the form of the ceremony sits in section 45 of the Marriage Act 1961, and the celebrant's explanation sits in section 46.
s45(2) block quote, word for word, linked to AustLII s45 and legislation.gov.au (C2004A07402).
s46(1) block quote, word for word, linked to AustLII s46 and legislation.gov.au; lead-in restates the fact only, no commentary.
A minister of religion may follow any form and ceremony recognised as sufficient by their religious body or organisation.
New Zealand: couples can write their own vows as long as each says words to the effect of 'I [name] take you [name] to be my legal wife/husband/partner' (linked to govt.nz source).
FAQ 'Can we write our own vows in Australia?': s45(2) words 'or words to that effect' are sufficient with a non-minister celebrant.
Advisor body line: one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel and vendors with you as your single point of contact, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
'1 to 2 minutes' stated only as our advice; examples timed by word count (longest 65 words, example 8 shortest at 39 words).
If you marry legally in another country, the legal wording follows that country (takeaway 4 and Marrying overseas).
